A sophisticated lived-in Manhattan apartment with curved walnut furniture, ivory upholstery, soft grey plaster walls, daylight and expressive shadows. Sculpture on a low dark console, not a tall gallery plinth. Flowing curved architecture echoes the sculpture. Composed architectural photograph with enough room context to understand placement. Camera at seated eye level, refined architecture publication photography, realistic materials and imperfections, no people, no text, no logos, no watermark, no additional sculptures. The sculpture must be fully visible, the main focal point but occupy only approximately 60% of the image height, with room context around it. Place the complete sculpture inside the middle 38% of image width so a central 3:4 mobile portrait crop retains the sculpture and some room context. Do not enlarge it into a monumental object; plausible tabletop/console sculpture scale. Avoid generic beige showroom, tall cube pedestal, exaggerated blur, oversaturated colours or fake luxury ornament.
